notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on: Thomas Garrity's assistant dates (1884-87 vs Pepper 1886); Patrick Garrity's end (1891 vs state marker 1885); fog-signal building demolition (1950s vs 1968); electricity (1940 vs 1940-52); stair count (138/130; Pepper counted 120 on his visit); tower height (record 33 m, 113 ft = 34.4 m to ventilator ball per museum society); distance from old light (a mile vs two); brick restoration cost; 1890 fog-signal delivery date; whether the light is still active. Hudson bottle, Metz fire, 1911 fire, Byrnes children anecdotes and 1902 Board quote are all second-hand via LighthouseFriends; the Board's 1902 report and newspapers for the fires were not read. Mary Garrity's 1913 obituary (OCR 'Mar j Garrity', '1RG1') matched to Mary by husband's 1861 appointment. Bulletin 1935 is OCR; Anna Garraty range-light years from it. Fog-signal figures from the 1891 and 1892 Board reports; printed page numbers unconfirmed, scan pages cited. 1900 report entry cited by number (no page index). Lighthouse Board reports for 1870-1890 and 1902-1910 are not in the local corpus. Sibling 'Katherine' not in roster. Source 13 unused. Thomas Garrity's age: Pepper says 18 in May 1886, the 1935 Bulletin says 65 at retirement in 1935 (born about 1870); the two do not agree. Post-1960 Coast Guard roster names left out (living-people rule). Printed page of the 1891 Board report fiscal-year page not confirmed; scan page cited. LighthouseFriends' $7,500 (3 March 1869) is for range lights, a different appropriation from Pepper's $7,000 of 2 March 1867 and the museum society's $7,500 dwelling estimate.
